note: Re-judged by an independent judge after the row's annotation moved from {not-applicable} to {gap}. RFC 9012 Sections 3.2.1 and 3.2.2 read 'The remaining bits in the 8-bit Flags field are reserved for further use. They MUST always be set to 0 by the originator of the sub-TLV.' The originator of a Tunnel Encapsulation attribute is a BGP speaker, Ze's declared role, and Ze already originates the attribute for SR Policy. VXLAN and NVGRE encapsulation is an absent feature, not a role Ze does not fill, and no owner decision declines it, so the earlier not-applicable verdict no longer stands and the row is a conformance gap. Ze builds no VXLAN or NVGRE Encapsulation sub-TLV: internal/component/bgp/plugins/nlri/srpolicy/config.go::buildTunnelEncap writes tunnel type 15 with the RFC 9830 sub-TLVs only. An operator can still originate one as a generic attribute 0x17: internal/component/bgp/textparse/rawattr.go::decodeTypedRawAttribute returns the opaque form for a code no keyword names, and attribute 23 has none, so Ze sends whatever Flags octet the operator wrote and nothing zeroes or refuses the reserved bits.
